title: Guys im struggling.
author: Separate-Honeydew-73
selftext: So im new to gamedev as a whole but im still trying and its so hard even w AI. Im using I tried to make an mma game but it looks terrible the animations dont sync (used maximo) and the character models look poor. AI isnt really doing much besides just backend stuff and even that its struggling to sync. Can i get any advice on what to do and also any idea on how to learn front end stuff like making environments character models synced animations. I want to have a character creator so how can i make a base character design and then have many hair options etc etc

comments.author: OurPillowGuy
comments.body:
You could not have picked a harder game to start with, except maybe an MMO. This game probably requires multiplayer, is heavily reliant on having multiple layers of complex animation systems, requires high detail characters closeup… and you want a character creator, which also incredibly difficult and content intensive… 

Build a walking sim first. Clone brick breaker as a first project. Hell, even building a single player FPS first would be easier than this. 

Games are really fucking hard to build, and the reality is that AI doesn’t just solve every problem for you. You still need to know how to scope, build, and finish a project.

replies.author: Separate-Honeydew-73
replies.body: thank you! ill start w easier projects. my intention wasnt multiplayer but more of a offline career mode thing. But ur right.

replies.author: Baphaddon
replies.body: Yeah a (reasonably complex) fighting game was the hardest game I’d ever made hands down.

comments.author: Saiss00
comments.body: Dont build a dream game. Start with small project first.

comments.author: hannemaster
comments.body: What exactly do you mean with animation don’t sync?

comments.author: Nervous_Teach_5596
comments.body:
Do the game same game, offline, 1 player, then go with the perilous path of connection, server updates, and their ugliness, network updates per ticks

Those things are the devil, even if you come with experience on programing, because you're playing and the server is playing, if you lose 1 tick, you will be almost dead or died on the next one, if the server don't have updated your tick on time

comments.author: NatalieKCY
comments.body: Don't do everything at once, split the game into smaller modular tasks and combine them later. It's easier/less rng to make smaller scripts work, and then merge the working ones. Don't focus on how it looks, focus on the game mechanics first, it's your MVP (minimum viabe product). You can swap the art assets later.

comments.author: loopywolf
comments.body:
I hear you man.

I am making a topdown 2D base builder and the one thing that drives me NUTS is that there are no tilesets and you can't generate the with AI =(

I must have wasted 4 weeks banging my head against that wall.. Now I'll just have to draw them all myself.

replies.author: Puzzleheaded-Way542
replies.body:
You can absolutely generate tilesets wirh ai image genration, like Gemini etc.

You wont get full pixel animated frames etc. But you can get at least 2 states easily where you just reload the tile and say how it should look in state 2.

Then you could have a go at doing the animation for the frames in between yourself. Its still a great way to get on with the game itself.

replies.author: loopywolf
replies.body:
Not pixel, and I don't require animation.  Just tiles, with seamless edges.

If you know how to do this, perhaps you could share a prompt?

replies.author: loopywolf
replies.body:
Direct top-down like Zelda or RimWorld.. NOT isometric.. They ALL do @#!@#! isometric

You begin to see the problem, I think =J

replies.author: loopywolf
replies.body: That looks pretty awesome! Could you please share your prompt?? Please?

replies.author: Puzzleheaded-Way542
replies.body:
I just asked for an overhead view of a compound. You will have better luck doing individual elements.

https://preview.redd.it/8d3qzaxsh69h1.jpeg?width=1080&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=4d279f81a338fad464d014d22c60f39129ff7208

replies.author: loopywolf
replies.body: And can you then generate tiles from this, i.e., wall tiles that repeat, grass tiles with seamless texture?

replies.author: Puzzleheaded-Way542
replies.body:
Yeah, I guess I would focus on one tile at a time, I feel like the more you ask for at once, the more likely it will shift perspectives to the most common tile types.
Glad it helped, you just need to play around, almost tricking them into doing what you want sometimes. 

The same prompts wont always work too.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
You picked a difficult project. Ai 3d animation is quite challenging

Someone made a 2d fighter and the animations are barely serviceable for that one.  (It is already a good attempt too)

replies.author: ffxivthrowaway03
replies.body: Yep, there's a reason nearly every asset generator out there is specifically pixel art.  It's big, blocky, and hides a lot of defects in the detail

comments.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
comments.body:
Using ai with an engine seems to work for me. I started with just asking chat gpt how to do this and that. Now I actually know at least a bit about Godot. Anti ai will tell you that you can’t make anything good ever if you use ai. The truth is a bit more nuanced I think. You can’t just prompt your way into making a good game…. Yet. 

Start really small and try to learn what the ai is doing as you go.

comments.author: d-czar
comments.body:
Watch a few of this guy’s videos if you want to learn about using AI to make and animate 3D assets. It’s not easy. But if you spent a bunch of time learning these new tools, it’s way more possible than it used to be. If you know what you’re doing, you can do things in days that would’ve taken months or years.
